label: Final copy step of length-4 sequences
explanation: Copy-phase-only feature: 99.8% of its activation mass falls on copy steps, and it is essentially silent in the original phase and on <DEL>. Its core is the last output step of length-4 sequences (t=7, where the model recalls orig(3) while orig(2) is the input). It fires on about 94% of those steps, and they hold about 70% of the mass, including all of the top activations. The strongest examples have orig(1)=r, so the previous input is r (prev_tok=r has 6.6x lift), which suggests a token-content effect on magnitude. Outside this core, weaker and sparser activations appear late in the copy phase of other lengths: L=5 at the last two steps, and L=8-9 at recall_idx >= 4 with to_go <= 4. Rates there are only 1-8% per step, so precision is low for any broader predicate. Overall 82% of the mass is at to_go=0. It does not fire on the first two copy outputs, in the original phase, or on the delimiter.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: r, h, k, p, y, j; least: <DEL>, q, v, w) and the current input token, by step (t=5: 0, m, l, e; t=6: 0, b, w, q; t=11: c, a, q, k); timing cues that raise it most: L=4 & t=7, t=6, recall_idx=4.
